reviewer: ChatGPT engineering author — not independent Pass C
method: Three source-bound 100-card commander-first specific proposed swaps; archived Oracle text checked separately

reviews.commander_first_role: Inalla's Eminence copies nontoken Wizards entering under its controller; bloodline/Ruthless Technomancer and Scholar/sacrifice-ritual lines should be efficient without spending mana to cast Inalla.
rules: Pitiless Plunderer is a Human Pirate, not a Wizard, so Inalla does not duplicate its ETB.

Pitiless Plunderer costs {3}{B} and generates one Treasure whenever ANOTHER creature you control dies. It does not make Treasure on its own death without replacement effects; the extra mana must be realized from actual creature deaths.
Blood Pet costs {B}, has a free sacrifice-to-add-{B} mana ability, fuels black-mana sequencing and graveyard/reanimation planning and can be sacrificed immediately; it is NOT a Wizard either.

Inalla's Eminence copying a Wizard token costs {1} for each nontoken Wizard ETB if Inalla remains in command zone or battlefield; extra Treasures might fund this, but measured creature-death timing and payoff is unverified.
reviews.strategic_cost: Four mana in a cEDH spells-and-Wizard combo deck replaces a one-mana immediately sacrificeable black mana resource; M5 test-pass is a mana-only proxy, not demonstrated acceleration of Spellseeker or Scholar loops.
reviews.positive_case: Treasure generation from repeated non-Plunderer Wizard token deaths could eventually refund repeated Eminence copies and support a long Bloodline/Technomancer recursion loop; the proposed candidate has thematic engine possibilities, but only with a properly verified creature death policy.
reviews.why_hold: No actual combo-by-turn, accessible four-mana Plunderer board, commander-dependent optimization, or proven improvement over low-curve Blood Pet sacrifice mana. An existing engine card is not expendable on raw late-game resource generation alone.
reviews.next_gate: Test a small exact legal Bloodline/Technomancer token-death loop with Inalla and Plunderer, check whether the Treasury effect supplies a new win line, compare realistic mana access to Blood Pet then submit independent Pass C review.

reviews.commander_first_role: Goad with Mark of the Rani on ETB/attack, profit Clues whenever goaded creatures damage your opponents, and monetize Clues with Manufactor/Illuminator/Time Sieve and artifact payoffs.
rules: Drafna's {1}{U} activated ability returns TARGET ARTIFACT YOU CONTROL to hand; bouncing an existing Clue token makes it cease existing instead of preserving it for replay.
Drafna's {3}, {T} copies a target ARTIFACT SPELL YOU CONTROL on stack; it does not copy already existing Clue tokens, Aura/Mark tokens, or investigate trigger instances.

An artifact spell copy resolves into a token permanent, but that special spell-copy arrival is not treated as creating a token by a token-creation effect for triggers that care about a token being created.

Curse of Opulence does not itself goad, but is a one-red-mana curse on a player; when the enchanted player is attacked, its controller creates a Gold token, and attacking opponents can create their own Gold. It promotes profitable forced combats that The Rani exploits for investigations.
Gold is an artifact mana token, not a Clue; Gold creation is not investigate, so Academy Manufactor does not replace Gold creation purely due to the Curse.
reviews.strategic_cost: Replacing low-curve combat-linked Gold incentives with Drafna's artifact spell-copy bounce package removes direct value from attacks against the cursed opponent; relevant repeated *artifact spell* casts and mana to activate Drafna are unmeasured.
reviews.positive_case: Drafna can rebuy ETB artifact permanents such as Five Hundred Year Diary and copy artifact spells. If a real mana-positive artifact recursion line engages Rani's Clue infrastructure, it may deserve testing against a different cut.
reviews.why_hold: Raw M5 Spellbook combo completions do not establish the necessary artifact-spell sequences in this exact approved goad deck; Curse of Opulence's combat-vs-artifact token role is distinct and coherent. No evidence the Drafna engine compensates for losing it.
reviews.next_gate: Reconstruct exact M5 claimed Spellbook interactions with all required pieces in deck, confirm whether copied ARTIFACT SPELLS trigger desired payoffs, compare game-state Gold + attack pressure versus Drafna's mana/turn costs.

reviews.commander: Nicol Bolas, the Ravager // Nicol Bolas, the Arisen
reviews.commander_first_role: Deploy Nicol Bolas, the Ravager; pay transform cost for a new back-face planeswalker object and then proliferate/copy loyalty activations, using planeswalker and Chain Veil infrastructure.
rules: Aetheric Amplifier costs {3}, taps for one mana of any color, and at sorcery speed with {4}, {T} can double the number of each kind of counter on target permanent. Loyalty counters on Nicol Bolas, the Arisen qualify.

Aetheric Amplifier costs at least three mana and then a further four mana and tap for the loyalty-doubling mode (on different priority windows if needed). It is not a zero-mana acceleration replacement.

Mox Diamond costs {0}; if it would enter, you may discard a LAND card instead, and only then enters and taps for mana of any color. This can enable early Bolas or the transform sequence when a land can be spared.

Bolas's transformation is a sorcery-speed activated ability on Ravager which exiles the creature and returns it transformed as a new permanent; it is a seven-mana ability before effects such as Training Grounds, but planeswalker loyalty activations are independent of summoning sickness.

Doubling counters on target permanent affects loyalty counters but does not create a planeswalker loyalty ability activation or grant an extra legal loyalty activation. A nonland permanent with zero counters stays at zero.
reviews.strategic_cost: Removing one of the strongest turn-zero colored accelerants can delay Ravager and the transformation by a turn or more. Aetheric Amplifier's sorcery-speed seven-mana total deployment-plus-activation is substantially slower even if it produces extraordinary Bolas loyalty late.
reviews.positive_case: The addition is unusually coherent for the Bolas superfriends identity: more loyalty counters improve the transformed Bolas ultimate and can combine with proliferation/doubling/copy abilities; separate non-Mox cut may be appropriate after efficiency review.
reviews.why_hold: The commander-specific upside is real, but choosing Mox Diamond as its cut sacrifices scarce acceleration in a deck whose commander needs four mana plus a costly transform. No paired timing evidence or other cut identified; retain canonical list.
reviews.next_gate: Compare the real three-mana deployment + four-mana loyalty doubling activation against existing Deepglow Skate, proliferate and Chain Veil slots; screen lower-impact non-mana candidates, model transform turn and actual loyalty payout; seek independent judgment and owner approval only if supported.
